---
title: "Sources"
---

`legal_provisions` builds the Markdown of one legal provision from any of four
sources. Which one answers is the package's one real decision.

| Source | How | When |
|---|---|---|
| **SCJN** | reads the law's consolidated text as it read right after this reform out of the `scjn-leyes` release, with no DOF request at all | the default, whenever the corpus covers this `codNota` with a link the project is certain of; `source="dof"` turns it off |
| **HTML** | converts the note's `cadenaContenido` HTML directly, with a DOF-tailored BeautifulSoup converter | the note has digital text; preferred, since it is clean, already scoped to the one note, and needs no OCR |
| **Image** | downloads the note's scanned page images through `dofjson`, OCRs them with `document2md` and mineru, then slices out the one note | image-only notes, or any note when the certified scanned original is wanted |
| **PDF** | downloads the note's own PDF (the edition PDF sliced to its pages, through `dofjson.download_nota_pdf`), OCRs it, then slices out the one note | when a PDF is preferable to page images |

Both OCR paths mirror the HTML path's output style (`#` and `##` headings,
`**bold**`, `*italic*`, GitHub tables), so a note's Markdown looks much the
same whichever source it came from.

## The SCJN path

The Court's legislative database keeps, for every reform of every federal law,
a snapshot of the law's consolidated text exactly as it read right after that
reform. Those snapshots are crawled through the SCJN's own SCOW JSON API,
matched to the DOF `codNota` that enacted them (see [Linking](linking.qmd)) and
published as the `scjn-leyes` release: 315 laws, 3,724 snapshots. A `codNota`
the release covers is answered straight out of it, which is what
[reconstruction](reconstruction.qmd) otherwise has to infer by replaying every
reform decree in order.

The SCJN is not an official source of legal text; the DOF is. Every file this
path writes therefore keeps the corpus' own provenance header (`fuente: scjn`,
`ordenamiento`, `fecha_publicacion`, ...) intact, and lands under a different
name, so the file alone says where it came from:

| | file written | with no `outdir` |
|---|---|---|
| SCJN path | `outdir/{slug}-{fecha}.md` (`lfca-05-01-1999.md`) | `<CACHE_DIR>/scjn-leyes/md/{slug}-{fecha}.md` |
| every DOF path | `outdir/nota-{codNota}.md` | `<CACHE_DIR>/dof/nota-{codNota}.md` |

The snapshot `scjn` writes carries the outline the SCJN's API states, one
`<!-- scjn:block ... -->` marker line before each block. nota2md reads the text,
not the outline: it takes the snapshot with the markers out
(`markdown_de_snapshot(..., outline=False)`), so what it returns is exactly the
text.

A `codNota` whose decree reformed several laws at once resolves to more than
one law and raises `ValueError` listing the candidates; `instrumento="<slug>"`
says which. A `codNota` the corpus does not cover, a law not on disk, or a
network failure reading the release all fall back to the DOF path, the last two
with a warning.

## Notes SIDOF does not have

SIDOF, the gazette's JSON service, is missing whole days of the gazette, and the
notes published on them have no SIDOF record at all: no `cadenaContenido`, and
no `codDiario` or page numbers for the OCR paths to start from. When SIDOF
answers an empty record for a `codNota`, `legal_provisions` looks the note up on
the DOF's own website instead, which serves the same HTML:

```bash
nota2md 4997808 --outdir output   # DOF 03-03-1999, a day SIDOF lost
```

The HTML path is the only one that can build these notes; asking for
`--source image` or `--source pdf` on one raises rather than fetching the wrong
pages.

## Cutting a note out of its page

A scanned page, or a sliced PDF, usually holds more than one note: it can begin
with the tail of the previous one and end with the start of the next.
`legal_provisions` uses the day's own index, which lists every note's title in
order, to locate two boundaries in the OCR'd text, where this note's title
appears and where the next note's title appears, and keeps only what lies
between. Matching is fuzzy (accent-folded, marker-stripped, `difflib`
alignment) to tolerate OCR differences, and it also drops the next note's
organism header that the DOF prints above its title. `--min-confidence` sets
how sure the match has to be before a boundary is applied; `--notas` sources
the titles from a saved day instead of fetching them.
